# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This book contains the **Open and Reproducible Science in R** workshop materials.
It introduces a connected research workflow using GitHub, renv, Docker, targets,
Quarto, pins, vetiver, and Zenodo, with a focused extension on responsible sharing
and differentially private synthetic data.

The practical examples and expanded teaching activities are under development.
The current R and pipeline helpers are placeholders.

## Getting started

Start with the [introduction](pages/1_introduction.qmd) for the learning objectives,
workflow, and prerequisites. Some familiarity with R will help you follow the
material. The [repository README](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r#usage-with-docker)
describes Docker setup and the available computing environments.

Use the book navigation to move between chapters. A PDF download is available
from the HTML book's download menu once both output formats have been rendered.
The PDF contains the same configured chapters in a single document.

## People and community

See the [coordinators](pages/2_coordinators.qmd) for presenter and co-author
information. Event dates and venues are listed in the
[workshop announcements](ANNOUNCEMENTS.md).

The community chapters contain contribution, accessibility, conduct, security,
and AI-assisted development policies, followed by the changelog.
